en.title: What Should You Do First in a Land Dispute?
en.directAnswer: Start by protecting evidence and identifying the real type of dispute. A land problem may involve ownership, possession, boundary, inheritance, fraud, a forged deed, mortgage or a government record. Do not use force. Collect documents, make a timeline and get the correct legal route for the facts.

atAGlance.whoFor: A citizen has a land conflict and needs safe first steps.
atAGlance.legalBasis: Land Crime Prevention and Remedy Act, 2023; applicable civil, criminal and land laws.
atAGlance.mainRule: The 2023 land-crime law contains offences relating to land fraud. A dispute can still be civil, criminal, administrative or a mix, so do not label every land disagreement as a crime.
atAGlance.updateStatus: Do not publish a one-size-fits-all “file this case” instruction.

en.lawMeaning: The 2023 land-crime law contains offences relating to land fraud. A dispute can still be civil, criminal, administrative or a mix, so do not label every land disagreement as a crime. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Photograph current possession and boundaries where safe.
Collect deeds, khatians, maps and mutation papers.
Save tax receipts and payment records.
Check whether forged documents or threats are involved.
Get legal advice before filing the wrong case.
evidence: Deeds; khatians; maps; mutation; tax receipts; photos; notices; messages; witness list; court papers if any.
en.simpleExample: A neighbour moves a boundary marker. Before fighting, the owner saves photos, gets the relevant map and records, and seeks the correct survey/legal remedy.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: destroying the other side’s property.
Common mistakes: filing a criminal complaint only to pressure a civil opponent.

whatIf.question: What if someone forged a deed?
whatIf.answer: Preserve the document and get legal help quickly.

whatIf.question: What if you are threatened?
whatIf.answer: Safety and police reporting may be necessary.

whatIf.question: What if a case is already in court?
whatIf.answer: Follow the court process, not GRS.

en.specialistTrigger: Threats or violence; forged deed; dispossession; injunction needed; court case; large-value property; unclear title.
